entries.content:
The for-each implementation is working. The trace shows two records being processed and both `{{data ...}}` placeholders being resolved.

The failure happens afterward while recording the completed action activity. [`listIgnoredPaths`](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/git/git_commands.js:250) executes `git check-ignore -z -- <paths>`, but Git permits `-z` only with `--stdin`. Activity persistence then fails and [`finishRunWithActivity`](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/action/action_run.js:468) changes the completed run to failed.

The tests missed this because they mock Git and explicitly expect the invalid arguments.

Proposed solution: implement the existing B_352 solution—remove `listIgnoredPaths` from normal persistence and use `includeProjectFolderInGit` plus `projectFolder` as the authoritative policy. Add a regression test using a real temporary Git repository. This fixes B_360 and the same underlying project-switch failure without introducing a separate workaround. No files were changed.
why is it doing anything with git?

Git is involved because md² stores action history in `design/activity/card__….json` and automatically commits that file after a run.

Before committing, the shared persistence code calls `git check-ignore` to avoid staging files intended to remain local. That check runs for every activity commit, even though it was introduced for the optional local-only project-folder behavior.

So for-each itself does not require Git. The loop completes, then history persistence reaches an invalid Git command and incorrectly marks the run as failed.
but why is it committing after every run?

Because md² treats action history as project data. Each run appends a record to the card’s activity JSON and commits it immediately so the history is versioned, shareable, and not left as an uncommitted change.

This is a general action-run persistence policy, not something required by for-each. Whether every run should create a Git commit is a separate design decision.
